title: History of the World in the 20th Century

sections.headline: War in Europe! America Vows Neutrality
paragraphs: Western Europe has fallen to the German Blitzkrieg, which now turns to invade the Soviet Union. President Roosevelt vows to keep America out of the war. The Japanese oil embargo is lifted even as their forces expand into mainland China. With Roosevelt’s focus on peace and neutrality, the secret “Manhattan Project” is quietly disbanded.

sections.headline: Hitler Assassinated! Germany Retains Control
paragraphs: After a disastrous, failed attempt to invade Britain, the frozen, starving German army is being ground down in the ferocious Battle of Moscow. The world is shocked when Hitler is assassinated by elements of the German high command. Even as de-Nazification proceeds, the celebrations are short-lived when it becomes clear that the new German leadership has no intention of relinquishing their battlefield gains.

sections.headline: United Europe and Pacific Reconciliation
paragraphs: Facing growing resistance movements across Europe, the Treaty of Berlin allows the restoration of national sovereignty across Europe while retaining German influence and supremacy. This paves the way for a formal alliance and a United Europe (UE).

The European treaty forms the basis for an armistice agreement between Japan and China. Japan agrees to withdraw from its increasingly untenable occupation in exchange for trade concessions, mutual non-aggression agreements, and an uneasy peace.

sections.headline: Russia Resurgent
paragraphs: Still recovering from catastrophic losses during WWII, Stalin has reorganized the remaining Soviet states into the Union of Eurasian Republics (UER). Vowing to never again be subject to a devastating invasion, the Union begins an armament campaign and aggressively absorbs neighboring nations.

sections.headline: African Forces Triumphant in Suez
paragraphs: President Nasser declares that Egypt is seizing control of the Suez Canal. Both UE and UER forces contest the move, but well-organized, well-equipped forces from Nigeria and the newly formed Pan-African Federation (PAF) push them back. The incident accelerates anti-colonial efforts in Africa and globally, signifying the emergence of a new global power.

sections.headline: Andean-Atlantic Confederation
paragraphs: Rejecting American influence and inspired by the rising African federation, Central and South American nations begin to form their own military alliance. A newly elected revolutionary government in Spain shocks Europe and the world by joining the new confederation. Argentine bombers arrive in Spain and deter the gathering UE armor divisions, formalizing the new Andean-Atlantic Confederation (AAC).

sections.headline: Greater Pacific Commonwealth
paragraphs: Years of trade and mutual-defense agreements have turned ancient rivalries in Asia into wary partnerships. The Australian government, increasingly isolated from Britain, proposes that the region's nations form a formal military and trade alliance: the Greater Pacific Commonwealth (GPC). Chile, increasingly at odds with AAC leadership in Brazil, opts to join its trade partners in the alliance.
India, finding itself surrounded by allied military powers, is forced to abandon neutrality and sign a mutual-defense agreement with the Pan-African Federation.

sections.headline: The Arctic War and North Atlantic Alliance
paragraphs: Using pressure campaigns, propaganda, and mass infiltration, followed by a sudden show of force, UER forces sweep in and seize control of Norway, Sweden, and the Alaskan territory.

The American populace is outraged. A new administration vows to end America’s non-intervention policies and fiercely defend American interests at home and abroad. The United States begins a massive rearmament campaign and signs an agreement with Britain to form the North Atlantic Alliance (NAA).

sections.headline: Growing Tensions
paragraphs: Simmering tensions ignite in skirmishes and standoffs worldwide. The American armada bound for Alaska is turned back by a GPC blockade. United Europe forces amass to challenge AAC and UER incursions. Across Africa and South America, the prevailing powers move to reclaim the last remaining colonies from foreign factions who vow to defend them.

sections.headline: Global Cataclysm
paragraphs: The world is divided among six great powers. Each of them is riven with ancient grievances, territorial ambitions, threatened borders, humiliating occupations, and entangling alliances.
The stage is set for World War III and a Global Cataclysm…
